subject: Consolidated econ checks + simulation plan for MAP
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily@clearsighthealth.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@clearsighthealth.com>, procurement@clearsighthealth.com
Date: 2027-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify MAP econ assumptions before exec review

David — thanks again for the demo yesterday. The execs asked us to confirm the MAP economics before our internal approval meeting next Friday. A couple quick asks so we can validate numbers on our side: 

- Can you confirm the tokens-per-$ assumptions for the hosted model variant in the MAP (you mentioned ~3.2k tokens/$ for the Llama2-13B quantized path). Is that peak throughput or amortized with batching?
- How are you modeling caching? Is prefix caching assumed for repeated user prompts, and if so what cache hit rates did you use for the simulation?
- For latency-sensitive flows we need expected p95 latency when batching at 8 vs 32.

I've attached our current MAP draft (light edits) — would appreciate a consolidated sim that uses our traffic mix (attached sheet tab: traffic_profile). If you can get a short PDF summary of the unit econ sims we can include it in the exec packet.

Thanks,
Emily
Director, Digital Ops
ClearSight Health

Attachments: clearsight_map_draft.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily@clearsighthealth.com>
Cc: Jason Lee <jason.lee@clearsighthealth.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-29T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify MAP econ assumptions before exec review

Emily — great questions, appreciate the heads-up on the exec packet. High level answers below and I'm looping in Laura and Ben for the sim exports. We'll deliver a 1-page PDF and an appendix spreadsheet by EOD Wednesday so you have time ahead of Friday.

- tokens/$: Our model uses a blended tokens-per-$ based on the quantized Llama2-13B path for steady-state hosted traffic. The value you quoted (~3.2k tokens/$) is the amortized figure at our current mix (50% short prompts, 30% multi-turn chat, 20% embeddings-heavy queries). We'll run the sim with a sensitivity range: 2.5k — 4.0k tokens/$.
- caching: Prefix/KV caching is modeled with two levers: session-level prefix reuse (for repeated user prompts) and application-level template caching (for identical prompt templates). Default hit-rates we use: 18% session prefix, 12% template — but we'll run scenarios at 5%, 20%, and 35% hit rates per your ask.
- batching & latency: p95 latency numbers depend on target batch sizes and the autoscaling profile. Rough ballpark at present: batch=8 -> p95 ~ 180–240ms; batch=32 -> p95 ~ 320–420ms. We'll include p50/p95/p99 in the sim outputs and annotate where batching causes tail-latency spikes.

I attached a short checklist of what we'll include in the PDF: baseline tokens/$, cache hit sensitivity, batching latency table, and a recommended MAP gating threshold for acceptance (units/$ floor + p95 SLA).

Best,
David Kim
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: unit_econ_sim_summary.pdf (draft)

Subject: Fwd: Clarify MAP econ assumptions before exec review — action items

Looping you in — Emily needs a concise PDF + updated spreadsheet for ClearSight's exec packet by EOD Wed (2027-05-03). Can we split tasks:

- Ben: run the sim suite with the ClearSight traffic_profile (attached) and export the scenarios: base (18%/12% cache), low-cache (5%/5%), high-cache (35%/25%). Include tokens/$ band and per-route token counts.
- Laura: produce the 1-page PDF summary (one table for tokens/$ sensitivity, one for batching latency p50/p95/p99). Add a one-line recommendation for MAP gating (suggest: tokens/$ >= 2.8k and p95 <= 350ms for batch=8).
- Neha: can you validate the pricing math against our current hosted rates and the Dedicated commit tables? Call out any notes for procurement/negotiation if ClearSight tries to lock a lower per-token baseline.

Please include at least one scenario that assumes a 10% uplift in conversational depth (avg tokens per session +10%) — they mentioned some pilot training prompts that are longer.

Thanks — I captured the deliverables in the spreadsheet and shared the link in the Drive folder. I'll consolidate and send to Emily once we have the PDF and the final workbook.

-David

Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify MAP econ assumptions before exec review — sim outputs ready

All — uploaded three scenario sheets to the Drive folder and exported the summarized CSVs. Quick notes from the sims:

- Base (18% session / 12% template cache): blended tokens/$ = 3,150 ± 7% (this accounts for mixed route weightings).
- Low-cache (5%/5%): blended tokens/$ = 2,720 ± 9%. Unit cost rises most for the embeddings-heavy route because we can't amortize KV-cache across those calls.
- High-cache (35%/25%): blended tokens/$ = 3,980 ± 6%.

Batching impact (p95) for Llama2-13B quantized path at target concurrency in their traffic profile:
- batch=8 -> p95 = 210ms (base), p95 = 260ms (low-cache with +10% tokens/session)
- batch=32 -> p95 = 370ms (base), p95 = 440ms (low-cache +10% depth)

I've flagged the scenario where depth + low-cache pushes cost above their internal threshold (we should include an ops recommendation: enable prefix caching on 80% of session-based flows and tune template reuse on the front-end).

Drive link to CSVs: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-Map-Econ-Sims

-Ben

From: Emily Zhang <emily@clearsighthealth.com>

David / team — thank you, this is exactly what we needed. The 1-page PDF is clear; execs appreciated the three cache scenarios and the explicit recommendation to gate on tokens/$ and p95 for batch=8. A couple follow-ups before I close this on our side:

- Can you add a brief note in the PDF that the simulations assume model fallback to a 7B variant only when Dedicated capacity is exhausted (i.e., not automatic at high load)? This was an exec question.
- Procurement asked if there is flexibility on the units/$ floor in a 12-month reserved commit — can Neha share a short note we can hand them?

If you can add those two lines, we'll attach the updated PDF to the MAP and move to internal approval. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Emily
Director, Digital Ops
ClearSight Health
